pr_title: Use single channel for homematic event subscriptions
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
During initialization of the homematic integration event subscriptions are set up for the parameters of the Homematic devices. In this step, the correct channel to listen to is selected. For some devices (e.g. Homematic IP covers), the same parameter is used in multiple channels. In this case the values shown in Home Assistant change rapidly and might (incorrectly) trigger automations. Please find related issues below in "Additional information"

This PR changes this behaviour by making sure only a single channel is being subscribed. A prioritization of the "nodes" is used, with SENSORNODEs having highest priority, and writing nodes, auch as Action/Event/etc, having lower priority.

Didn't have a deeper look at it. But wouldn't this break state-updates for devices that share a parameter across multiple channels? Like IO-devices with a `STATE` parameter on multiple channels, which produces the same amount of switch-entities. This is currently working, and would be a regression if after applying this patch only the first relevant channel keeps working.

In regards to your actuator, I think the correct solution would be to actually also add the other two actor-channels as entities, and the status-channel as a sensor-entity.

> Didn't have a deeper look at it. But wouldn't this break state-updates for devices that share a parameter across multiple channels? Like IO-devices with a `STATE` parameter on multiple channels, which produces the same amount of switch-entities. This is currently working, and would be a regression if after applying this patch only the first relevant channel keeps working.
> 
> In regards to your actuator, I think the correct solution would be to actually also add the other two actor-channels as entities, and the status-channel as a sensor-entity.

I actually don't think that the patch influences this kind of devices with intentional multiple channels. Those would have multiple channels inside a single "node", e.g. WRITENODE = [3, 7, 11]. These cases are (before and after the patch) handled by the `if len(...) == 1` else-case, using the self._channel. That I did not change. 

What this changes is just the case where the same parameter (e.g. LEVEL) is defined in (e.g.) SENSORNODE (LEVEL = [3]) and WRITENODE (LEVEL = [4]). These cases would now be reduced to use only the prioritized SENSORNODE, avoiding to subscribe to multiple channels for the same parameter and entity. If the node has multiple channels defined (e.g. [3, 7, 11]), all of them will still be kept (and then overwritten by  self._channel).

The only deduplication happens in the creation of channel_dict, which deduplicates the keys (such as LEVEL), but does not touch/change the value (which could still be a list of multiple channels).

issue_context.title: Homematic HmIP-BROLL state toggles randomly
issue_context.body:
## The problem
Since updating Home Assistant to 0.114.x / 0.115.x states of HmIP-BROLL covers toggle randomly from "open" to "close" (or vice versa) when covers are not completely opened or closed. This was not the case in HA releases prior to 0.114.x.

This happens without covers moving at random intervals ~3-4 times per hour.

State changes to new state and back to old state within less than 0.5 sec.

No errors or warnings in either HA Core log or in HomeMatic add-on log.

This causes notifications regarding cover state being triggered and filling up HA logbook without cover changing state in reality...

## Environment
- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.114.x / 0.115.x
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 0.113.3
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): HassOS 4.13
- Integration causing this issue: HomeMatic CCU version: 10.3 (CCU firmware: 3.51.6 (latest add-on release) / HmIP-BROLL firmware 1.6.2)
- Link to integration documentation on our website:
https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/homematic/
https://github.com/home-assistant/hassio-addons/tree/master/homematic

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
```yaml
homematic:
  interfaces:
    rf:
      host: core-homematic
      port: 2001
      username: Admin
      password: !secret homematic_password
    wired:
      host: core-homematic
      port: 2000
      username: Admin
      password: !secret homematic_password
    hmip:
      host: core-homematic
      port: 2010
      username: Admin
      password: !secret homematic_password
```

## Problem-relevant HomeMatic add-on configuration
```yaml
wired_enable: false
hmip_enable: true
rf:
  - type: CCU2
    device: /dev/ttyAMA0
wired:
  - serial: xy
    key: abc
    ip: 192.168.0.0
hmip:
```

For me this looks like channel 3 reporting the correct value (35 in this case) triggering a state change, while channel 4 at the same time reports 0 as a value which triggers another state change.

That at least explains, why I see these state changes happening, but still the question that remains is, why the behavior is different in 0.113.3 compared to 0.115.2?

The reason for the different behaviour of 0.113 and 0.115 is this tiny change introduced in pyhomematic 0.1.68:
https://github.com/danielperna84/pyhomematic/pull/319/commits/6e8f05fedf27ebea23e2f11ef7d7700e706a45c2

It adds channel 3 to SENSORNODE and therefore an event listener is now created for channel 3 as well, in addition to channel 4 which was already being listened to as it is listed in WRITENODE.

As we (now) know, channel 3 is the only channel we should listen to for those HMIP cover devices. Channel 4 holds the target state, not the actual, and is not updated when you e.g. stop the cover manually via the wall switch. That's exactly the behaviour you see. 

Solution: listen to changes/events on channel 3 (SENSORNODE) only for this device. Easier said than done, as the code that adds event listeners is common among all Homematic devices, and does this for WRITENODE as well, but I have an idea and might add a PR for this in the next few days.
